outcomes: A consumer learns that a stream was refused from the HTTP status, before it has parsed a single event
A provider cannot outrun a slow consumer or write a frame the consumer contract requires it to reject
A stream that produces nothing for a while stays distinguishable from a dead one
nonGoals: Serving the WebSocket transport of the same endpoint
Resuming a stream the consumer lost

requirements.text: A server-stream endpoint decides admission before the first body byte: a request that carries a body and a request whose params or query do not validate are refused with a non-2xx status, never with a 200 followed by a terminal event. Past admission the provider bounds what it writes — queue depth and frame size are declared, and exceeding either fails the stream with the typed terminal event — and it writes liveness comments that carry no data so a quiet stream is not read as a dead one.

A first-party server stream that declares a continuation acknowledges a request that asks for putnami.sse.v1 on the admitted response head and ends it with the exact complete frame once the handler returns, every message was written and the consumer stayed. A failure ends it with the typed error, a cancellation or a draining provider with nothing, and a request that does not negotiate, or a route without a continuation, keeps the legacy framing byte for byte.
